html:
Vytautas the Great ruled the Grand Duchy of Lithuania from 1392 to 1430, when it was the largest state in Europe, stretching from the Baltic almost to the Black Sea.

He was a grandson of Gediminas and fought his cousin Jogaila, King of Poland, for years before they agreed that Vytautas would rule Lithuania. In 1410 they defeated the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Grunwald, one of the largest battles of medieval Europe. He settled Tatars and Karaites in Lithuania, where their descendants still live.

He was to be crowned king in 1430 but died before the crown arrived. Lithuanians remember him as their greatest ruler. His castle at Trakai, near Vilnius, has been rebuilt. See Lithuania.
